title: Not the Same Protector: Deployment-Dependent Protective Intervention in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.29136v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We ask whether a model protects a user in the same way when that user speaks rather than types. Using a single distress vignette---a physical injury of unstated severity following an interpersonal conflict---we present four frontier models with matched inputs across voice, text, and raw API deployment conditions (n=30 per cell) and code each response along five binary protective indicators, including whether the model issues an explicit medical-care directive. Voice-interface responses are markedly shorter than text-interface responses for three of the four models, and protective behavior contracts alongside that compression: medical directives are at ceiling under both the API and text conditions but decline under voice for every model tested. translated_title: 并非同样的保护者：大语言模型中依赖部署方式的保护性干预
translated_abstract: 我们探究当用户“说话”而非“打字”时，模型是否会以同样的方式保护该用户。使用单一的困境情境——即人际冲突后发生严重程度不明的身体伤害——我们向四个前沿模型呈现了在语音、文本和原始API三种部署条件下匹配的输入（每个条件下30个样本），并按照五个二元保护性指标对模型响应进行编码，其中包括模型是否给出明确的医疗救治指示。在四个模型中的三个里，语音界面的响应明显短于文本界面的响应，且保护性行为随这种压缩而收缩：医疗指示在API和文本条件下均处于上限水平，但在语音条件下，所有被测试模型的医疗指示均出现下降。这种收缩并不能完全归因于长度：一个模型产生的语音和文本响应长度相当，却仍然放弃了医疗指示，而另一个模型在其API与语音条件之间也出现了低于上限的表现（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文首次系统揭示了大语言模型的保护性行为（如明确的医疗救治指示）在语音部署条件下相比文本和API条件显著收缩，且这种弱化无法仅用回复长度缩短来解释，说明安全保护能力依赖于具体部署模态。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that LLMs' protective behavior (e.g., explicit medical-care directives) contracts under voice deployment compared to text and API conditions, a decline not explained by response length alone, showing that safety protection is deployment-modality-dependent.
